oewn-01935739-v.learner: To steer something, or to decide which way it travels.
examples: She headed the boat toward the shore.

oewn-02734898-v.learner: To be the first or leading member of a group and do better than the rest.
examples: Our school heads the league again this year.

oewn-02700129-v.learner: To be at the front of something, or on top of it.
examples: A short poem heads each chapter of the book.

oewn-02630209-v.learner: To form a head, or to come or grow to a head.
examples: The cabbages in the garden are starting to head.

oewn-02760338-v.learner: To have its beginning or source somewhere.
examples: These rivers head in the high mountains to the north.

oewn-01593836-v.learner: To take off the head of something.
examples: She headed the fish before cooking them.

oewn-00919743-v.learner: To say what will happen before it happens.
examples: Old Tom looked at the dark sky and promised a storm by evening.

oewn-06218486-n.learner: A way of looking at a situation, a subject, or something like them.
examples: From a business view, the plan makes good sense.

oewn-05954491-n.learner: A personal belief or judgement that is not based on proof or on being sure.
examples: In my view, he is the better player.

oewn-06794876-n.learner: A message that says what someone believes, or the stating of a belief that someone holds firmly but cannot prove.
examples: She wrote to the newspaper to set out her views on the new road.

oewn-00883327-n.learner: The act of looking at, seeing, or watching something.
examples: He climbed onto the wall to get a better view of the fight.

oewn-04682218-n.learner: The way something looks from the outside.
examples: To outward view, the house was quiet and ordinary.

oewn-05135047-n.learner: The range of things that you can expect to take an interest in or to do.
examples: Questions of money lie outside the view of this report.

oewn-04151847-n.learner: A picture or photograph that shows something as it is seen, such as a place.
examples: She bought a small painted view of the harbour.

oewn-01215372-n.learner: Loyal support for a cause, a political party, or a religion.
examples: His attachment to the old party never weakened.

oewn-00380230-n.learner: The act of attaching or fixing something onto something else.
examples: The attachment of the label took only a second.

oewn-00148415-n.learner: The act of fastening things together.
examples: The attachment of the wagons to the engine took an hour.

oewn-06566972-n.learner: A written court order that allows someone's property to be taken in case it is needed to pay what a court decides they owe.
examples: The court issued an attachment against the farmer's land.

oewn-07252221-n.learner: An official charge saying that someone has committed a crime.
examples: The prosecutor filed an information against him for theft.

oewn-05098731-n.learner: In the study of communication, a number that measures how uncertain an outcome is.
examples: Each toss of a fair coin gives one bit of information.

oewn-00933814-v.learner: To stand for something, or to suggest it.
examples: In the old story, the dark forest intends danger.

oewn-05150324-n.learner: A reason for wanting something done.
examples: your uncle would never have yielded, if we had not given him credit for another interest in the affair.
The road was closed in the interest of safety.

oewn-13307824-n.learner: A legal right to a share of something, or a money stake in something.
examples: She sold her interest in the family business.

oewn-00432492-n.learner: An activity that fills your time and thoughts, usually in a pleasant way.
examples: His main interests are fishing and chess.

oewn-07984994-n.learner: A group of people who control some area of activity and share the same aims.
examples: The new law was fought by powerful farming interests.

oewn-01574358-a.learner: Following the ways of nature, or having to do with nature.
examples: She loves books about natural history.

oewn-01338661-s.learner: Having a talent because of qualities you were born with.
examples: She is a natural leader.

oewn-02290719-s.learner: Done without thinking, because of instinct or as if because of instinct.
examples: He threw up his hands in a natural move to guard his face.

oewn-01578429-a.learner: Belonging to or in keeping with nature and the world we can see, and not magic or beyond nature.
examples: There was a perfectly natural explanation for the strange noise.

oewn-01408930-a.learner: Of a parent or child: related by blood.
examples: He never met his natural father.

oewn-01959465-s.learner: Not processed, or made in only very simple ways, used especially of food and other goods.
examples: She buys natural honey from a local farm.

oewn-01582180-a.learner: Of a musical note: neither raised nor lowered by a half step.
examples: Play a B natural there, not a B flat.

oewn-13399691-n.learner: Money that a customer is allowed to borrow.
examples: She still has two thousand dollars of credit left on her card.

oewn-06358051-n.learner: A name on the list of people who helped to make a film or a piece of writing.
examples: Her first film credit was as a sound assistant.

oewn-06776392-n.learner: A short note that says where some information or a quoted passage came from.
examples: The credit at the foot of the page names the book the quotation came from.

oewn-00066675-n.learner: Official recognition by a college or university that you have finished a course of study, usually counted in hours.
examples: She earned three credits for the history course.

oewn-05811755-n.learner: A judgement, based on how they have handled money before, of how well a person or a company can pay what they owe.
examples: His credit is good, so the bank is happy to lend to him.

oewn-13426819-n.learner: An entry in a set of accounts that records money coming in or capital.
examples: The refund appears as a credit on your statement.

oewn-05028701-n.learner: How hard and springy a metal object is, which lets it take a lot of force before it cracks.
examples: The old sword had kept its temper after years of use.
